editorial:
Imagine coming home to find your spouse cheating and losing your cool so badly that you end up in prison. That is how your journey begins with the main character here. Once he gets out, he is a broken man who doesn't want to talk to anyone. He opens a small barbershop and spends all his time chatting with a pet eel he kept from his jail days. It is a strange setup, but the vibe is surprisingly cozy and human. You get to see a guy who feels totally alone try to figure out how to live in a world that might never forgive him.

What really works is how the movie shows his slow growth as he meets quirky neighbors who push him out of his shell. The acting is top-notch, and the slow pace makes you feel like you are really getting to know the characters. While some parts might feel a bit slow, the payoff is totally worth it. If you want to see it, I suggest grabbing the 4K Blu-ray for your physical collection to see the colors pop, or you can just rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night. It is perfect for anyone who likes a deep story about second chances.
endingExplained: At the end, the man finally stops hiding from his past and opens up to the people around him. He realizes that keeping the eel as his only friend was just a way to avoid the pain of real human connection. He eventually lets the eel go, which shows he is ready to move on. He finds peace with his mistakes and starts building a real life with the people in his town.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves character studies and stories about starting over.
